items.title: 2027: Adebutu pledges LG autonomy, border community dev’t in Ogun
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has reiterated his commitment to prioritise local government autonomy, grassroots development and strategic investment in border communities if elected in the 2027 governorship election. Adebutu made the pledge during a PDP campaign rally in Remo, Ogun State, where he outlined key elements of his ‘Itura De’ agenda, which he said was designed to return power to the people and strengthen development at the grassroots. The PDP candidate said local governments should be empowered to address the specific needs of their communities and determine development priorities without undue interference. According to him, functional local government autonomy would enable grassroots administrations to respond more effectively to the concerns of residents and deliver projects that directly improve their living conditions. He said: “Local governments must be empowered to address the needs of their people and determine the development priorities of their communities. Governance should be felt at the grassroots, where its impact matters most to ordinary citizens.” Adebutu also highlighted the importance of developing border communities, arguing that targeted investments in infrastructure and economic activities could unlock their potential and strengthen their contribution to Ogun State’s economy. He noted that Ogun’s proximity to Lagos presented significant opportunities for economic integration, trade and investment, adding that the state could benefit from stronger economic connections with its neighbouring commercial hub. According to him, improved infrastructure and deliberate economic planning would help border communities attract investment, create employment opportunities and contribute more meaningfully to the state’s overall development. Also speaking at the rally, the PDP’s Ogun East senatorial candidate, Alhaji Abdul-Hameed Femi Omotayo, called for visible and measurable development across the senatorial district. Referring to his visit to Sagamu two days earlier, Omotayo said his observations during the visit had raised concerns about the town’s development trajectory. He criticised what he described as inadequate progress, using a metaphor to contrast urban development with the condition he said he encountered in the town. “The current administration has turned town to bush instead of turning bush to town,” he said. Omotayo’s remark underscored his concerns about the pace of development in Sagamu and the need for projects that residents can see and feel in their daily lives. He maintained that Ogun East needed tangible results in infrastructure, employment generation and the creation of opportunities for residents, particularly young people. The senatorial candidate also stressed the importance of addressing challenges affecting economic activities across communities in the district. Poor road infrastructure, limited employment opportunities and inadequate access to economic opportunities remain important issues in discussions about community development. Deteriorating roads can increase transportation costs and impede the movement of goods, while a shortage of jobs can restrict the options available to young people. items.title: Ghana must pursue BRICS partnership if it brings economic benefits – Kpebu
items.description: Legal practitioner and analyst Martin Kpebu says Ghana should pursue a partnership with the BRICS economic bloc if it offers tangible economic benefits to the country. He argues that Ghana’s foreign policy should be guided by national interest rather than an exclusive alignment with traditional Western partners. Speaking on TV3’s The Key Points, Mr Kpebu said the country must be willing to explore opportunities with different international partners, just as major global powers pursue relationships based on their own interests. “I support Ghana becoming a partner, as long as it brings us economic development. We don’t have much so if there is something to be gained from it, why not?” he said. His comments come after Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced that the government had decided to formally apply for Ghana to join BRICS. The government says the move is intended to diversify Ghana’s international partnerships, expand economic opportunities and strengthen cooperation with countries in the Global South. Mr Kpebu dismissed concerns that Ghana’s engagement with BRICS would automatically undermine its longstanding relationship with the United States. He noted that Ghana and the US have maintained diplomatic and economic ties over several decades, arguing that those relationships would not necessarily collapse because Ghana sought cooperation with other economic blocs. “The U.S. is not going to run out of Ghana overnight because we join BRICS,” he said. According to him, Ghana’s engagement with alternative economic partners could also encourage traditional allies to attach greater value to their relationship with the country. He argued that international relations are driven largely by national interest, and Ghana should adopt a similar approach in determining its partnerships. “What do we gain by continuing to say, ‘Oh, we are with the U.S., we are with the UK, so we can’t join BRICS?’” he asked. Mr Kpebu further compared international relations to competition for attention, suggesting that Ghana’s willingness to explore other partnerships could strengthen its position in dealings with existing allies. He clarified that his support was for Ghana pursuing partner status with BRICS rather than necessarily seeking full membership immediately. “ As long as we’re going to get benefits, let’s go for it,” he said. BRICS, originally formed by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, has expanded to include additional members. The grouping seeks to strengthen economic cooperation and increase the influence of emerging economies in global affairs. Mr Kpebu’s comments add to the debate over how Ghana can pursue new economic opportunities while managing its existing diplomatic relationships.

items.title: Interview – Dr Oubeidallah Hlal : « Le Maroc à l’Olympia doit devenir un véritable rendez-vous culturel à Paris »
items.description: Après une première édition à guichets fermés, « Le Maroc à l’Olympia » revient le 16 novembre prochain dans la mythique salle parisienne. Dans un entretien accordé à Hespress FR, le Dr Oubeidallah Hlal, cardiologue, humoriste et producteur à l’origine de cet événement, revient sur les ambitions de cette deuxième édition, les nouveautés attendues et sa volonté de faire rayonner la culture marocaine à l’international. Entre musique, humour et partage, il évoque également le rôle de la culture dans le rapprochement entre le Maroc et la France. Hespress FR : Après le succès de la première édition, qu’est-ce qui vous a poussé à relancer « Le Maroc à l’Olympia » et quelles nouveautés souhaitez-vous apporter à cette deuxième édition ? Dr Oubeidallah Hlal : La première édition nous a surtout montré qu’il y avait une vraie envie de se retrouver autour du Maroc, de sa musique, de son humour et de toute cette énergie qui nous rassemble. On a vécu quelque chose de très fort avec le public et, à la fin de la soirée, on a tout de suite senti que cette aventure devait continuer. Pour cette deuxième édition, on veut évidemment garder l’âme de la première, mais aller encore plus loin. Il y aura de nouvelles rencontres artistiques, davantage de surprises et surtout plusieurs univers et plusieurs générations qui vont se croiser sur scène. L’idée est vraiment de proposer un grand spectacle autour de la richesse de la création marocaine. Et puis il y a aussi une ambition qui dépasse cette seule soirée : faire du Maroc à l’Olympia un véritable rendez-vous culturel à Paris, un événement fédérateur qui puisse s’inscrire dans la durée et contribuer, à notre échelle, au rayonnement du Maroc. À travers la musique et l’humour, vous souhaitez faire rayonner la culture marocaine à l’international. Quelle image du Maroc souhaitez-vous transmettre au public français et à la diaspora marocaine ? Je veux montrer le Maroc tel que je le ressens : un Maroc vivant, moderne, ouvert sur le monde, mais profondément attaché à son identité et à ses racines. Notre richesse, c’est justement notre diversité. Il n’existe pas une seule musique marocaine, une seule génération ou une seule manière de raconter notre pays. Le Maroc est pluriel, et cette pluralité fait partie de sa force. Sur la scène de l’Olympia, on veut réunir différentes sensibilités artistiques et différentes générations, tout en faisant passer un message commun : celui d’un Maroc uni, fier de sa culture et tourné vers l’avenir. Pour les Marocains du monde, il y a évidemment une dimension très émotionnelle. Pendant quelques heures, au cœur de Paris, on retrouve des sons, des références, de l’humour, des artistes et une ambiance qui nous ramènent au Maroc. Et pour le public français qui connaît moins cette culture, j’aimerais que ce soit aussi une porte d’entrée pour découvrir un Maroc contemporain, créatif et généreux. Pouvoir raconter cette image du Maroc sur une scène aussi emblématique que l’Olympia, c’est une immense fierté pour nous. Vous présentez également « Le Maroc à l’Olympia » comme un espace de rapprochement entre les Marocains du monde et un moyen de renforcer les liens entre le Maroc et la France. Quel rôle la culture peut-elle jouer dans ce dialogue ? La culture a cette capacité extraordinaire de rapprocher les gens très naturellement. On peut avoir des parcours, des générations, des origines ou même des langues différentes et pourtant se retrouver autour d’une chanson, d’un éclat de rire ou d’une émotion. Entre le Maroc et la France, les liens humains, historiques et culturels sont extrêmement forts. Il y a aussi toute cette génération de Marocains et de Franco-Marocains qui vit entre ces deux cultures et qui constitue un véritable pont entre les deux pays. Le Maroc à l’Olympia veut justement faire vivre ce lien de manière positive et très concrète. Pendant quelques heures, Français, Marocains, Franco-Marocains ou simplement amoureux du Maroc se retrouvent dans la même salle et partagent les mêmes émotions. C’est là, à mon sens, toute la force de la culture : elle crée du dialogue sans avoir besoin de grands discours. Et si cette soirée peut, à son niveau, contribuer à renforcer encore les liens culturels et humains entre le Maroc et la France, alors nous aurons aussi réussi quelque chose d’important. Vous êtes à la fois cardiologue, humoriste et producteur. Comment cette diversité de parcours nourrit-elle votre vision de « Le Maroc à l’Olympia » et votre manière de porter ce projet culturel ? Ce sont effectivement trois univers très différents, mais finalement ils ont tous un point commun : l’humain. En médecine, on apprend à écouter les gens et à être attentif à ce qu’ils ressentent. Dans l’humour, on apprend à les observer, à comprendre ce qui les touche, ce qui les rassemble et évidemment ce qui les fait rire. Et dans la production, il faut réussir à transformer une idée et une envie en quelque chose de concret et surtout de collectif. Tout cela influence forcément ma manière de porter Le Maroc à l’Olympia. Je ne veux surtout pas que ce soit simplement une succession d’artistes qui viennent chanter ou faire rire sur scène. Je veux que la soirée ait une âme, qu’elle raconte quelque chose du Maroc et qu’elle fasse ressentir quelque chose au public. C’est un projet auquel je suis très attaché personnellement. Il y a bien sûr le spectacle et le divertissement, mais derrière, il y a cette volonté de célébrer notre culture, notre diversité, notre unité et de participer à son rayonnement au-delà de nos frontières. Si, à la fin de la soirée, les gens repartent heureux, fiers pour certains, curieux d’en découvrir davantage pour d’autres, et avec le sentiment d’avoir vécu un vrai moment de rassemblement autour du Maroc, alors pour moi, le pari sera réussi. items.title: ITF J100: America’s Wright wins J100 Accra Girls’ Singles Title
items.description: Third-seeded American Sydney Wright proved unstoppable at the ITF J100 Accra, concluding a six-week tournament run by defending her girls’ singles title in a thrilling final against Zimbabwe’s Kuzivaishe Chappa. Wright reached her second consecutive Accra final after beating Poland’s top seed Alisha Ndukwu in a dramatic three-set semifinal. Following her victory over Ndukwu in the previous week’s championship match, a long, three-hour and 40 minute battle. Wright showed great confidence once again. In a tough match lasting 2 hours and 48 minutes, the American fought back from a set down to win 5-7, 6-2, 6-3. Standing in Wright’s way was Chappa, who delivered a strong performance to eliminate seventh seed Parish Nikhil Shinde of India. The Zimbabwean won a close first set in a tiebreak before Shinde took the second. Staying focused on the final set, Chappa got a late break to claim a hard-fought 7-6(4), 4-6, 6-4 victory. For Chapepa, reaching the singles final offered a chance at redemption after losing a close double final the week before alongside her sister, Kudzai Erin Patience Chapepa, against Ndukwu and Yelyzaveta Kolesova (7-6(4), 6-3). In the Girls’ Singles final on October 10, Sydney Wright proved too strong, defeating Kuzivaishe Chappa in a fast and dominant performance giving Chappa no space to breathe in a 6-2, 6-0 victory to claim back-to-back J100 Accra Girls’ Singles titles. The singles triumph completed a doubles sweep for Wright, who also lifted a trophy on October 9, alongside her doubles partner Ogunjobi, defeating top seeds Milana Kolesova and Alisha Ndukwu with a convincing 6-3, 6-1 win. Now a multiple titleholder, Sydney Wright’s dominant week highlighted the big dreams of these rising young stars, who continue to chase global success, break barriers and inspire the next generation of tennis players across Africa and around the world. Organised by Tennis Foundation Ghana in partnership with the Ghana Tennis Federation. The ninth edition of the ITF Juniors World Tennis Tour came to an exciting end at the National Tennis Centre, Accra Sports Stadium.

items.title: Expedition hopes to find aviator Amelia Earhart’s plane on remote island
items.description: A team of researchers are on their way to a remote island to inspect what they think could be the wreckage of famed aviator Amelia Earhart’s plane. The group, from the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University, are expected to arrive at Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean by Monday in the hopes of solving the mystery of her disappearance. The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation on her fate. The team are aiming to find what has been called the Taraia Object, first spotted sitting on the edge of a lagoon off Nikumaroro in satellite imagery in 2020. Purdue University said the object had since been confirmed to have been visible in aerial photography of the area dating back to 1938. The researchers are currently roughly halfway through their journey to the remote atoll aboard the Marin Mainiku, a Kiribati National Shipping Line vessel. They departed the capital of Kiribati on Wednesday to begin the 830-mile journey to Nikumaroro, which is also part of the multi-island country. When they eventually arrive, they will have to navigate through a narrow gap created in the atoll’s reef created by the British in 1963 – the last time the island was inhabited. “Finding Amelia Earhart’s Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime,” Richard Pettigrew, head of the ALI and the expedition lead, said. Earhart had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her Electra twin-engine plane when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea on 2 July 1937. From there, she and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to travel towards Hawaii and then finally back to California. But her plane vanished without a trace while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote, uninhabited coral island near Nikumaroro, to refuel. Earhart’s disappearance spawned numerous theories – from a simple crash due to fuel exhaustion to more elaborate claims of interference. The official explanation is that the plane suffered communication problems while the two struggled to find the island, and Earheart eventually crashed into the ocean when she ran out of fuel. While this version of events is largely accepted, no physical evidence has ever been recovered. One theory is that Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway. Images of the so-called Taraia Object show what could be the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters. But some – including rival explorers – have expressed scepticism that this could be a plane, let alone Earhart’s. Ric Gillespie, who specialises in recovering historic aircraft wrecks, told news agency Reuters that the object looked like a tree that had fallen from the atoll into the nearby water. “I’d love to find that airplane. It ain’t gonna happen,” he said. The researchers en route to the island credit Gillespie with previously finding evidence of a human presence on the atoll in the 1930s and forensic analysis of skeletal remains found there in the 1940s they say lend credence to their theory. But Gillespie suspects Earhart’s plane had likely broken apart and its fragments carried into the depths of the Pacific long ago. Previous attempts to find her Electra have also come up short. In 2024, a group of researchers said they may have found it lying around 4,877m (16,000ft) below the surface near Howland Island through sonar imaging – but this was later confirmed to be a rock formation. Similarly, an expedition in 2019, conducted by the marine archaeologist who discovered the Titanic wreck, to investigate a photograph of what might have been a landing gear protruding from the water near Nikumaroro also failed to find anything.

items.title: Gordon nets first Barca goal as Liga leaders beat Getafe
items.description: Anthony Gordon scored his first goal for Barcelona as the Spanish champions extended their perfect start in La Liga with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday. England international Gordon opened the scoring in the second minute and Gabriel Jesus added another after half an hour for the league leaders, who have won every match they have played this season. French defender Jules Kounde tucked home the third from Lamine Yamal’s cross to cap Barca’s solid win against Jose Bordalas’s side at Camp Nou. Barca moved five points clear of second-placed Atletico Madrid, who won 2-1 at Alaves earlier, and lead Real Madrid, fourth, by nine points before Los Blancos host Villarreal later on. Barca were without their top scorer Raphinha, who sustained a hamstring problem during the international break with Brazil. Flick replaced him with former Arsenal striker and Selecao compatriot Jesus and his side came roaring out of the blocks. Gordon, who has impressed since joining this summer, grabbed his first Barca goal with a low deflected effort after bundling his way past three players. The winger was Barca’s brightest spark in the first half, continuing his fine goalscoring form for England in the recent Nations League matches. Barca defender Eric Garcia forced a save from Getafe goalkeeper David Soria with a drive from distance as Flick’s side controlled the game. Getafe defender Zaid Romero gave the ball away in his own box for Barca’s second, passing it straight to Jesus, who stroked into the bottom corner. Soria denied Olmo before Yamal teed up Kounde for the third. The defender, making a record 194th appearance for Barca for a French player, overtaking Eric Abidal, was on hand to turn home from close range from teenage star Yamal’s cross. Barca, who also won their Champions League opener, have nine victories from nine matches across all competitions. items.title: États-Unis : l’ouragan Isaias frappe la Floride, des vents violents et des inondations redoutés
items.description: L’ouragan Isaias a touché terre vendredi soir en Floride, avec des vents soutenus atteignant 165 km/h. Les autorités redoutent des dégâts importants, des inondations et de fortes vagues alors que plusieurs États du sud des États-Unis ont déclenché des mesures d’urgence. L’ouragan Isaias a atteint les côtes de la Floride vendredi 9 octobre au soir, a annoncé le Centre national américain des ouragans (NHC). Classé en catégorie 2 sur l’échelle de Saffir-Simpson, qui en compte cinq, le phénomène s’accompagne de vents violents et de fortes précipitations. Avant même l’arrivée de l’ouragan, les premières rafales avaient commencé à frapper Pensacola et ses environs. Des toitures auraient été arrachées sur certaines habitations et commerces, tandis que des arbres et des branches ont été violemment secoués. « Nous prenons cette tempête très, très au sérieux », a déclaré le gouverneur de Floride, Ron DeSantis, qui s’attend à des « dégâts considérables » dans les zones côtières du nord-ouest de l’État. Face aux risques liés aux vents destructeurs, aux fortes pluies et aux vagues, plusieurs États bordant le golfe du Mexique, notamment la Floride et l’Alabama, ont décrété l’état d’urgence et ordonné des évacuations. Des perturbations importantes dans le secteur énergétique Le passage d’Isaias menace également les infrastructures énergétiques de la région. Plusieurs plateformes pétrolières ont évacué leurs employés, notamment celles exploitées par Chevron et Shell. Selon les données citées par l’agence américaine, environ deux tiers des capacités de production pétrolière de la région et plus de la moitié des capacités de production de gaz étaient suspendus vendredi. Près de 1,5 million de barils de pétrole brut par jour auraient ainsi été retirés du marché mondial. Plusieurs aéroports de Floride ont également temporairement interrompu leurs activités. La présence de nombreuses raffineries dans la zone fait craindre de nouvelles perturbations sur un marché énergétique déjà sous tension en raison des conflits au Moyen-Orient et en Ukraine. Un premier ouragan après une saison jusque-là calme Isaias est le premier ouragan de la saison à toucher les États-Unis continentaux depuis deux ans. La saison cyclonique dans l’Atlantique, qui s’étend généralement de début juin à fin novembre, avait jusqu’ici été inhabituellement calme. Cette situation s’explique notamment par l’influence d’El Niño, un phénomène climatique qui tend à limiter la formation des cyclones dans l’Atlantique tout en favorisant leur développement dans le Pacifique. Les autorités météorologiques américaines prévoyaient toutefois une diminution de l’intensité d’Isaias après son arrivée sur les terres. Elles ont néanmoins appelé la population à rester particulièrement vigilante face aux risques liés aux vents, aux précipitations et aux inondations. items.title: US seeks changes to rejected $109m health compact with Ghana – Mahama
items.description: The United States is seeking to revise its proposed $109 million health compact with Ghana, including amending or removing clauses that led to its rejection by Cabinet, President John Mahama has disclosed. Speaking at a citizens’ engagement in Goaso in the Ahafo Region, the President said the US government has requested further discussions on the agreement “The health compact the Americans brought to us, I have talked about it when I was in New York, so everyone knows about it. Later, they came back and said they wanted us to sit down and discuss the clauses we object to in the compact, with a view to either amending or removing them. We will sit down with them and discuss,” he said Ghana rejected the proposed agreement after raising concerns about provisions relating to sensitive health information, national sovereignty, counterpart funding and the regulatory authority of the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA). The proposed compact was intended to provide approximately $109 million in US health assistance over five years, replacing some funding previously received through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). At a dialogue hosted by the Council on Foreign Relations in New York on September 25, 2026, President Mahama explained why Cabinet rejected the proposed compact. He said Ghana had followed its established procedures, with the Ministry of Health reviewing the document and submitting an information paper to Cabinet. The review identified provisions the government considered problematic. One major concern was a requirement for Ghana to provide the United States with its pathogen profile, which contains information about disease-causing organisms circulating in the country. The President also objected to provisions he said required Ghana to share medical records. “It states that we shall give the United States our pathogen profile. I’m sure there are medical experts who understand that better than me. And it also says we should give our medical records. I mean, who takes another country’s medical records?” he asked. President Mahama further said the agreement required Ghana to commit its own funds to the programme while restricting the FDA’s authority to inspect medicines and other medical products brought into the country under the arrangement. Describing the conditions, he said, “I mean, it was humiliating.” He added that Cabinet rejected the agreement with government deciding it would not proceed with it under the proposed terms.

items.description: « Il est desormais moins cher de reserver un lancement standard de Falcon 9 (74 millions de dollars) que de faire transiter un VLCC [un petrolier geant] de l'USG [region de la cote du Golfe du Mexique] vers l'Extreme-Orient (~80 millions de dollars) », a ecrit sur X la compagnie de courtage maritime Gibson. Here's a fact to drive home just how incredible the current tanker market is: It is now cheaper to book a standard Falcon 9 launch ($74m) than it is to take a VLCC from the USG to the Far East (~$80m). #OOTT #tankers — Gibson Shipbrokers (@shippingenergy) October 8, 2026 Une situation qui resulte d'une « penurie mondiale de petroliers » qui « s'aggrave a chaque baril de petrole supplementaire transitant par le detroit d'Ormuz », a vulgarise Bloomberg, qui a repere cette publication. a titre de comparaison, s'il faut desormais depenser 77 millions de dollars pour affreter un grand petrolier, selon le Baltic Exchange de Londres, il n'en fallait que 9,2 millions en 2025. Le 2 octobre, Reuters rapportait que le coût d'affretement d'un grand petrolier, apte a transporter deux millions de barils, s'elevait a 1,2 million de dollars par jour , contre 80 000 dollars un an auparavant. Selon la societe de courtage Simpson Spence Young (SSY), a egalement souligne l'agence americaine, « meme en tenant compte de l'inflation, les tarifs actuels sont les plus eleves depuis l'arrivee des premiers superpetroliers sur les oceans dans les annees 1960, surpassant meme les niveaux atteints lors des conflits petroliers des annees 1980, lorsque l'Iran et l'Irak attaquaient la navigation commerciale dans le golfe Persique ». La presse specialisee pointe du doigt les frappes tant en Iran qu'en Russie. Au Moyen-Orient, les mois de tensions autour du detroit d'Ormuz, les recentes frappes des Houthis contre les installations saoudiennes, ont augmente les risques planant sur les navires tout en les poussant a changer leurs itineraires. L'offre de navires est d'autant plus resserree qu'une partie des petroliers a ete placee sous sanctions occidentales.

items.title: Trump Is an Easy Mark for Putin
items.description: Late last night, President Trump announced a “massive” deal to buy diesel fuel from Russia. For the American truckers and farmers Trump claims to be serving, the deal means little or nothing. Trump may not know or may not care that his latest gambit will not reduce diesel prices. His poll numbers are plunging to Herbert Hoover levels. He needs a last-minute electioneering gimmick. But while the deal will not benefit American consumers, it has immense consequences for others. For Vladimir Putin’s Russia, the deal is a potential lifesaver. For war-ravaged Ukraine, it is the most outrageous and heartless Trump betrayal to date. For Trump’s entourage, the deal promises corruption opportunities on a multibillion-dollar scale. And for people trying to understand the Trump presidency, the deal is further proof of the accusation that Nancy Pelosi flung in Trump’s face in 2019: “With you, all roads lead to Putin.” The United States is a diesel superpower. It is one of the world’s largest producers and exporters of diesel fuel. U.S. refineries produce about 5.2 million barrels of diesel a day. Americans consume about 3.7 million barrels a day. The surplus is sold abroad: In recent months exports have run above 1.5 million barrels a day. The United States imports some diesel fuel from Canada, about 154,000 barrels a day, owing to the peculiarities of pipeline and shipping networks: It’s cheaper to supply New England from the Canadian refinery in New Brunswick than from U.S. refineries along the Gulf Coast. By comparison, Trump’s Russia deal is for 2.25 million barrels : the equivalent of about 16 hours’ worth of U.S. consumption, 10 hours’ worth of U.S. production, or 14 days’ worth of Canadian imports. Unfortunately for U.S. diesel consumers, the price of diesel fuel is set by global markets, not North American ones. Trump’s Iran war has disrupted fuel supplies from the Middle East, including diesel supplies. Before the war, Europe imported more than half a million barrels of diesel a day from the Persian Gulf. The world’s second-biggest diesel exporter used to be Russia, which shipped about 817,000 barrels a day in 2025. When the Iran war raised energy prices, Russia was positioned to profit. [ David Frum: Why Trump didn’t predict the gas-price spike ] The United States in the past tried to help Ukraine by sanctioning Russian energy exports. Trump sometimes pretended to support this policy. In September 2025, for example, Trump proclaimed a tariff on India, ostensibly to punish India for buying Russian oil—but then lifted it in February. So the Ukrainians took matters into their own hands. As Russia has intensified its horrific drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian civilians, Ukraine has struck back with a devastating campaign against Russian energy infrastructure, including diesel. By late summer 2026, the Ukrainians estimated that they had shut down 43 percent of Russian refinery capacity. According to Ukrainian reports, Russian production of oil of all kinds plunged from 5.6 million barrels a day before the Iran war to 4.1 million barrels by late summer 2026. Russia imposed a ban on diesel exports in July. That ban has been extended into October. Friends of Ukraine hailed the attacks on Russian energy infrastructure as a war-changing success. Trump saw a threat to Republican hopes in the midterms. Curbs on Russian fuel exports helped push the price of diesel fuel in the U.S. above $5 a gallon in July, then higher than $6 a gallon in September. Since Trump’s return to power in 2025, the Putin regime has dangled lucrative deals in front of the president’s entourage. The Wall Street Journal reported in November 2025 about secret conversations in Miami the previous month between the head of Russia’s sovereign wealth fund, Kirill Dmitriev, and Trump’s negotiators, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: “For the Kremlin, the Miami talks were the culmination of a strategy, hatched before Trump’s inauguration, to bypass the traditional U.S. national security apparatus and convince the administration to view Russia not as a military threat but as a land of bountiful opportunity, according to Western security officials. By dangling multibillion-dollar rare-earth and energy deals, Moscow could reshape the economic map of Europe—while driving a wedge between America and its traditional allies.” The report noted that Dmitriev “found receptive partners in Witkoff—Trump’s longtime golfing partner—and Kushner, whose investment fund, Affinity Partners, drew billion-dollar investments from the Arab monarchies whose conflict with Israel he had helped mediate.” The New York Times reported last week about an even more brazen Russian offering: a multibillion-dollar oil deal for assets owned by Russia’s Lukoil, which would directly benefit a Trump donor and two Middle Eastern groups that have done business with Kushner or Witkoff’s family. (A spokesman for Steve Witkoff said of the Times story that Witkoff “has no conflict of interest and no financial stake in this matter.” Of the Wall Street Journal story, a source described as “familiar with Witkoff’s thinking” said “the envoy is confident that any settlement with Russia would benefit America broadly, not just a handful of investors.”) But all these apparently enticing Russian schemes come with a catch: Russian energy assets are not worth much if those assets are regularly wrecked by Ukrainian drones. This makes plain the implicit quid pro quo in these lucrative deals offered to Trump’s family and friends: If you compel Ukraine to surrender, we will enrich you beyond reckoning. Putin is attempting to leverage Russia’s most strategic asset in his war on Ukraine: Trump’s weakness for corruption. The 2.25 million barrels of diesel Putin offered Trump will have zero net impact on world energy markets or the world price of diesel. But accepting those barrels will collapse the U.S.-led sanctions regime on Russia—and align Trump with Putin against the Ukrainian air attacks on Russian energy production. Trump stopped providing aid to Ukraine long ago. But the U.S. still provides Ukraine with crucial intelligence information. If Putin can entice Trump to cut Ukraine off from U.S. intelligence, he can do real damage to Ukraine’s capabilities. Russian diesel fuel is the cheese in that mousetrap. Trump’s negotiators are sniffing at the bait: The Kyiv Post reported today that Witkoff and Kushner are already threatening to stop information-sharing if Ukraine continues to strike Russian energy assets. And meanwhile, FBI Director Kash Patel is reportedly planning his own trip to Russia—one that members of Congress are urging him to cancel, as my colleague Sarah Fitzpatrick recently reported . There is much about Putin’s offer of diesel that remains doubtful. Does Trump have the legal authority to buy previously sanctioned Russian oil? Does Russia even possess the diesel to sell? But one thing at least remains as clear as ever: With Trump, all roads lead to Putin.

items.title: Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi district for a month over 'threat to law and order'
items.description: The Rawalpindi deputy commissioner on Saturday announced that Section 144 had been imposed in the district for a period of 30 days, over threats to sensitive installations and other critical infrastructure. Section 144 is a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure which empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons. It has been imposed amid the PTI’s long march , which has so far remained within Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, but had initially announced to move towards the federal capital. The KP chief minister reiterated today that he would lead the convoy towards Islamabad. According to a notification seen by Dawn , the District Intelligence Committee (DIC) in a meeting today warned the DC of an “imminent threat” within the district to sensitive installations, major roads and other infrastructure “which may pose a serious risk to human life, public property, and the overall peace and order of the district”. “The DIC has reported specific intelligence suggesting that certain groups and elements are actively mobilising with intentions to disturb the law and order situation through large gatherings, protests, and disruptive assemblies,” the notification read. Moreover, the committee indicated that these elements may mobilise “individuals with the potential to engage in violent actions” against soft targets and near key installations and other sensitive sites. Imposing Section 144, DC retired Captain Nadeem Nasir prohibited public gatherings of more than five people, as well as the open display of weapons, improvised explosives, spikes, laden batons, gulails, ball bearings, petrol bombs, or other instruments that could cause physical harm. It also banned the use of drones and any attempts to “remove any restriction” imposed by the police to regulate assemblies and traffic. The order is set to expire on Nov 8. Section 144 has already been imposed in several parts of the country, with Islamabad imposing the provision for two months in a notification dated September 18. The order prohibited gatherings of five or more people, as well as processions, rallies and demonstrations, at any public place within the revenue limits of the district, including the Red Zone. Similarly, Section 144 is in force in Lahore until Oct 15, with the order citing serious threats to public peace, tranquillity and the safety of life and property. According to a notification issued by the Punjab Home Department, a complete ban was imposed on assemblies, processions and gatherings of five or more persons at public places, roads and open spaces. However, the ban would not apply to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, mosques and other places of worship, courts or government institutions.

items.title: Okpebholo, Wike, Oshiomhole, others honour Orbih at funeral
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu THE governor of Edo State, Senator Monday Okpebholo, Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and Senator Adams Oshiomhole were among the prominent politicians present when the remains of former Vice Chairman South -South of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Daniel Orbih, were on Saturday laid to rest in his home town, Ogbona, Etsako Central Local Government Area. Speaking at the funeral service held at St. John the Baptist Catholic Church, Ogbona, Governor Okpebholo tasked Nigerians, particularly those in positions of authority, to live selfless and sacrificial lives and use their positions to make society a better place for all. The governor, in an emotional voice, said the death of Orbih had reminded him of the uncertainty of life and the need for people to make meaningful contributions to society while they are alive. He recalled that his first visit to the church was to celebrate Orbih’s birthday and expressed sadness that he had returned to the same venue to attend his funeral. “This is my second time coming to this Church. The first time I came here was to come celebrate with Chief Dan Osi Orbih. I said to him, we will be coming here like this in the next eight years to celebrate your birthday but today we are here for a different purpose. “Today, it has dawned on me that there is nothing in life; here lies in the casket the remains of Chief Dan Osi Orbih and he can’t stand up or walk anymore,” he said. Wike, in his remarks, said the funeral activities had reinforced the reality of death and the pain of losing a close friend. “When I saw the casket, it dawned on me that truly my friend and brother is gone. There is nothing we can do but to pray to God to give the family the fortitude to bear this great loss,” he said. In his homily, the Catholic Bishop of Auchi Diocese, Most Rev. Dr. Gabriel Dunia, urged the congregation and Nigerians to reflect on the transient nature of life and the inevitability of death. Dunia said titles, academic qualifications, positions, social status and personal achievements could not prevent death when the time came. He called on the faithful to follow the path of truth and light, stressing the importance of living meaningful lives and remaining conscious of their responsibilities to God and humanity. “Death is what all must pay and one can tell God to hold on because we are busy at the moment but be prepared to answer the call at any time,” he said. The post Okpebholo, Wike, Oshiomhole, others honour Orbih at funeral appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: [Vidéo] Amboura : des girafes et des oryx en plein Fouta
items.description: Sur 1 050 hectares, dans le département de Podor, des girafes, des zèbres et des oryx vivent en liberté, sans qu'on leur distribue de nourriture. Créée en 2016 près de Thillé Boubacar, la réserve d'Amboura a vu sa population de cervicapres passer de cinq à 122 individus. Elle espère devenir d'ici 2027 une destination touristique, à condition de franchir les trois kilomètres qui la séparent de la route nationale. Dans le nord du Sénégal, dans le département de Podor, on n'imagine pas croiser des girafes. C'est pourtant ce que propose la réserve animalière d'Amboura, un espace de 1 050 hectares créé en 2016 au sein d'une forêt classée. Pendant l'hivernage, la réserve se couvre de hautes herbes, et acacias et jujubiers reverdissent. Le reste de l'année, elle retrouve des teintes plus sèches, plus proches de l'image classique du Sahel. Cette végétation est l'un des acquis du projet : après des années de protection, plusieurs espèces typiques de la région, comme les acacias et les balanites, se régénèrent et contribuent à la solidité des sols. Une faune libre et diversifiée Le principe d'Amboura est simple : les animaux ne sont ni parqués ni nourris par l'homme. Ils se déplacent à leur gré, cherchent l'ombre aux heures chaudes et vivent à leur rythme. La réserve accueille des espèces réintroduites, notamment l'oryx algazelle, devenu son emblème, mais aussi des girafes, des zèbres, des gnous, des cobes, des cervicapres, des élands et des autruches. Elles cohabitent avec la faune locale : phacochères, chacals, singes patas et petits mammifères de la région. Les oiseaux y trouvent aussi refuge, dont certaines espèces menacées, comme la grande outarde. Amboura relève donc autant de la conservation de la biodiversité que de la présentation de grands animaux. Amboura n'est pas un zoo, et rien n'y garantit l'observation d'un animal en particulier. Le meilleur moment pour la visite reste la matinée, quand la chaleur n'a pas encore poussé la faune à l'ombre. Il faut accepter que la nature décide du spectacle, et c'est en partie ce qui fait le charme du lieu. La réserve ne vit pas en vase clos. Elle emploie des gardiens issus des villages voisins et met son forage à la disposition des habitants pour abreuver leur bétail. Elle leur fournit aussi de la paille, un prélèvement qui profite à la régénération du couvert végétal. Des projets pour l'avenir Le principal frein reste l'accessibilité : quelques kilomètres de piste séparent la réserve de la route nationale, et la fréquentation demeure très faible. L'amélioration de cet accès est annoncée, ainsi que l'étude d'un hébergement en bois, discret et intégré au paysage, sur le modèle des camps de safari d'Afrique de l'Est et d'Afrique australe. L'ambition est de faire d'Amboura une destination d'écotourisme qui offre aussi des emplois, notamment de guides, aux jeunes de la zone. Reste à voir si la réserve tiendra ses promesses sur le long terme. Ses responsables parlent d'un premier vrai bilan dans dix à quinze ans. Oumar Boubacar NDONGO (Vidéo et texte) et Assane SOW (Photo)

items.title: Nine dead in mass shooting at Pennsylvania home
items.description: A man has shot and killed eight people, including two children, at a home in the US state of Pennsylvania before appearing to take his own life. Police were called to a street in the city of Erie on Friday afternoon after witnesses reported seeing a man firing a gun before he entered a home, the Erie News Now outlet reported. Two women were reportedly found dead in the street. The gunman then barricaded himself inside as police surrounded the building and ordered him to leave, but more gunshots were heard, the outlet reported. When police entered, several more victims were found along with the gunman , who had an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. The nine deaths were confirmed in a statement issued on Saturday by the mayor’s office. “Investigators have determined that all deaths occurred before officers arrived,” it said. “The deaths were not the result of any prolonged standoff or delay in police action.” Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said that “there are no words that can adequately express the magnitude of the loss of life here. He added that police “will not speculate about a motive or any information that could compromise this investigation”. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said he had offered his administration’s “full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night – killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians”. “My heart breaks for this family,” he said, adding that he and his wife “are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community”. The mayor is expected to hold a press conference on Saturday afternoon.

items.title: ‘Time for Ukraine to get new president,’ says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
items.description: US President Donald Trump has said he thinks “it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president” as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky’s criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia. Zelensky warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war in Ukraine. Speaking to the media as he left the White House on Saturday, Trump said the Ukrainian president “wants to make problems for the world” by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries. “He’d better damn well stop,” Trump said before suggesting Ukraine should “get a new leader who can make a deal”. Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs. “We said, ‘you can do whatever you want to Russia, don’t hit the refineries’, because that’s a world problem that’s caused,” he said. “He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does.” Trump confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April. Zelensky reacted by saying the relaxation of the penalties will allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war. He also accused Moscow of taking the deal “to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities” following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia. On Saturday the EU’s foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas echoed Zelensky’s criticism, saying suspending sanctions “provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war”, adding: “This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won’t.” She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday. The deal with Russia is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war. That conflict, which began in February, has sent the cost of petrol and in particular diesel skyrocketing, which has soured his standing with the American public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation.

items.title: Les nouvelles opportunités de l’économie durable au Sénégal
items.description: Dans le sillage d’un entretien accordé au quotidien « Le Soleil » par le Professeur Théophile Zognou, président du Consortium africain des fonds pour l’environnement (Café), Olivier Santi, associé gérant de Cristal capital, un fonds d’investissement basé à Genève, donne quelques pistes pour attirer des capitaux pour le financement de la biodiversité. À son avis, le Sénégal dispose d’atouts considérables : ses mangroves, ses ressources halieutiques, ses Aires marines protégées (Amp) et ses écosystèmes terrestres constituent un capital naturel essentiel à la sécurité alimentaire, à la protection du littoral, au tourisme et à l’activité économique.C’est pourquoi il estime que la préservation de ce patrimoine doit être envisagée comme un investissement de long terme et non comme une simple charge environnementale. « Comme tout capital, il doit être protégé, entretenu et valorisé durablement, en associant en priorité les populations locales qui doivent trouver un intérêt économique direct à sa préservation », explique M. Santi. Pour lui, les fonds fiduciaires pour la conservation offrent un modèle éprouvé pour articuler capital naturel et capital financier. Cela, en faisant converger les intérêts économiques, environnementaux et sociaux. Leur ancrage local permet, à son avis, d’associer les communautés à la protection et à la valorisation de leur patrimoine tout en sécurisant les financements à long terme. À Dakar, les travaux préparatoires à la création d’un fonds fiduciaire de conservation, présentés, à Bissau, par Wetlands International et ses partenaires, constituent une avancée concrète pour évaluer les besoins et structurer les financements. À Bissau, les fonds fiduciaires africains ont affirmé leur volonté de renforcer leur autonomie, de diversifier leurs ressources et de mobiliser davantage de capitaux sur le continent. Quelques jours plus tard, à Genève, les rencontres internationales Building Bridges, consacrées à la finance durable et qui vont du 6 au 8 octobre 2026, ont fait écho à cette ambition : passer des engagements aux investissements en mobilisant les capitaux autour de projets structurés et adaptés aux réalités africaines. « De Bissau à Dakar en passant par Genève, une même dynamique est à l’œuvre : faire converger les initiatives, les compétences et les capitaux, pour que la préservation du patrimoine naturel devienne un véritable moteur de développement économique durable au Sénégal », conclut Olivier Santi. Seydou KA

items.title: Accord Poutine-Trump sur le diesel : l’Ukraine prise de court, la poursuite des négociations avec les États-Unis annulée
items.description: Les negociations entre les etats-Unis et l'Ukraine a Miami ont ete ecourtees ce 10 octobre apres l'annonce de l'accord energetique entre Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump. Selon le Financial Times , la delegation ukrainienne, prise de court par cette decision sur les livraisons de diesel russe, a annule la deuxieme journee de discussions et abrege son sejour aux etats-Unis. Cet accord, annonce a l'issue d'un entretien telephonique le 9 octobre entre les deux presidents , prevoit la livraison de 300 000 tonnes de diesel russe des octobre, puis de 500 000 tonnes en novembre et d'un million de tonnes supplementaires par la suite. Selon le vice-Premier ministre russe Alexandre Novak, les exportations pourraient atteindre trois millions de tonnes par mois a terme. Washington a egalement accorde une derogation temporaire aux sanctions americaines, valable jusqu'au 7 avril 2027. Washington reclame l'arret des frappes contre les raffineries russes L'accord intervient alors que l'administration Trump reclame depuis plusieurs semaines la fin des attaques ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes. Selon Axios, Volodymyr Zelensky aurait ignore environ six demandes americaines en ce sens. Washington considere que ces operations contribuent a la hausse des prix des carburants aux etats-Unis et souhaitait leur arret sans contrepartie. Kiev proposait de son cote de suspendre ses frappes a condition que Moscou mette egalement fin aux attaques contre les infrastructures energetiques ukrainiennes. Mais selon Axios, Donald Trump ne considerait pas ces deux types d'operations comme equivalents. Les discussions a Miami avaient pourtant commence dans un climat presente comme constructif. Les representants americains et ukrainiens avaient notamment aborde des garanties de securite, des questions territoriales et les conditions d'un eventuel reglement du conflit. La poursuite des frappes contre les raffineries russes a neanmoins constitue un point de friction. Selon un responsable ukrainien, l'emissaire americain Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, gendre de Donald Trump, auraient averti Kiev d'une possible suspension du partage de renseignements si ces operations continuaient. Trump remet en cause la position de Zelensky Malgre les demandes americaines et l'accord energetique entre Moscou et Washington, Kiev entend poursuivre ses frappes contre les installations petrolieres russes. Selon le Financial Times , un haut responsable ukrainien a confirme cette intention. Donald Trump a parallelement durci ses critiques envers Volodymyr Zelensky. Le president americain a estime que l'Ukraine avait besoin d'un nouveau dirigeant capable de negocier un accord avec la Russie. Il a egalement reproche a Zelensky d'avoir laisse passer plusieurs occasions de mettre fin au conflit. De son cote, Moscou maintient sa disponibilite pour des discussions avec Washington sur les questions energetiques et les perspectives d'un reglement du conflit, comme l'illustrent les echanges entre les deux presidents. Les desaccords entre les etats-Unis et Kiev restent cependant importants, notamment sur la poursuite des frappes contre les raffineries russes.

items.title: Lutte contre la criminalité urbaine : La Police Nationale démantèle un réseau de présumés braqueurs dans le Djôrô
items.description: Le Service Régional de la Police Judiciaire (SRPJ) du Djôrô, avec le concours de la Division des Investigations Criminelles (DIC) de la Direction de la Police Judiciaire (DPJ), le Commissariat Central de Police (CCP) de la ville de Bogandé et la Direction du Matériel et du Budget (DMB) de la Direction Générale de la Police Nationale (DGPN), a mis fin aux activités criminelles d’un groupe de malfrats, en majorité des repris de justice, spécialisés dans les vols à main armée. Ils opéraient dans plusieurs localités du Burkina Faso, ainsi qu’à l’extérieur du pays, notamment Diarkadougou, Ouagadougou, Pouytenga, Houndé, Pâ, Dano, Diébougou, Bouroum-Bouroum, Legmoin, Kampti, Doudou, Gaoua, Bousséra, Galgouli, Bantara, ainsi que Doropo et Bouaké. Le gang était bien structuré et bien organisé où le rôle de chaque membre était bien défini. Relativement à son mode opératoire, ses membres procédaient à l’identification de leurs cibles qui sont principalement les lieux de commerce, les boutiques Orange Money, les fonderies d’or, les acheteurs d’or, les stations-services et autres établissements susceptibles de détenir des liquidités. Dès qu’une cible était choisie, ils se réunissaient dans un lieu pour préparer leur opération en déterminant les participants et les moyens à mobiliser. Pour passer à l’acte, ils se déplaçaient en binôme à motos et se masquaient avec des cache-nez, des casquettes et des pullovers. Une fois sur les lieux, ceux armés de fusils assuraient le guet et la sécurité du groupe, pendant que les autres, munis d’armes blanches, procédaient au dépouillement des victimes. Ils effectuaient généralement des tirs de sommation pour intimider les riverains et empêcher toute intervention, et n’hésitaient pas à abattre leurs victimes en cas de résistance. Après l’opération, une partie du butin était prélevée comme prix de location des armes et le reste était partagé entre les membres selon le degré de participation de chacun. Les téléphones portables volés étaient généralement abandonnés pour éviter d’être localisés par les enquêteurs, l’argent constituant leur principal objectif. Grâce à la collaboration des populations, les enquêteurs ont appréhendé quatorze (14) membres actifs du groupe et saisir plusieurs objets dont deux (02) fusils à pompe, un fusil de chasse, quatre (04) pistolets automatiques, des chargeurs, des munitions, des armes blanches, un véhicule, des motos et des appareils électroménagers. La Police Nationale remercie encore une fois les citoyens grâce à qui ce résultat a été atteint. Elle les invite par ailleurs à demeurer toujours vigilants autour d’eux, à éviter, autant que possible, de conserver d’importantes sommes d’argent dans les lieux de commerce et de faire preuve d’une vigilance accrue lors des déplacements ou des opérations financières. Elle les exhorte à poursuivre la dynamique de dénonciation des cas suspects aux numéros verts que sont les 17, 16 et 1010. La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens ! Source : Page Facebook de la Police Nationale

Hincapie injury adds to Arsenal issues after Guimaraes rescue act
items.description: For the second time in three Premier League matches, Bruno Guimaraes has come to Arsenal’s rescue. Having sparked their 2-0 win at Sunderland in September with the crucial first goal, the £75m summer signing came off the bench again to have a pivotal impact against Leeds on Saturday. This time it was the winner as the Gunners came from behind for a 2-1 success in a testing encounter at Emirates Stadium. But Ecuador international Piero Hincapie was carried off during the warm-down, raising concern the defender has suffered an injury. He came on as a late substitute against Daniel Farke’s side but completed extra running after the final whistle – a practice most clubs use. A fifth win in six league games put Mikel Arteta’s side level on points with leaders Manchester City, but their title defence has certainly not been without its scares so far. Following on from their comprehensive 3-0 defeat at Brighton last time out, Arsenal fell behind in a league match for a third time in four league matches – and only a David Raya penalty save stopped them from trailing at Sunderland as well. For large parts of the game against Leeds, they were nowhere near their best but, after going behind in the 55th minute, Riccardo Calafiori and Guimaraes – on his full home debut – secured an important three points. “It was a great game of football. Leeds were brilliant for one hour.” said Ally McCoist on TNT Sports. “Mikel Arteta made changes when he needed to and the substitutions gave Arsenal what they needed. That’s what champions do. Leeds can hold their heads high.” By getting wins when below par the mark of champions or are there reasons for concern for Arteta and Arsenal? Figure caption,Mikel Arteta post match interview – Arsenal vs Leeds United Guimaraes raises level after Brighton woe Coming into the season as defending champions, Arsenal were looking to make a statement signing to make their rivals take notice. They did not bring in the attacker they wanted but Guimaraes looks like he could be that key arrival to help Arteta’s men build on their success. The 28-year-old midfielder is a ‘win-now’ signing in the peak years of his career. He responded well to a disappointing performance in the defeat by Brighton, where he made his full league debut. The Brazilian international has now scored two goals that have helped his side to valuable points and justified the decision to spend big on Guimaraes, even if the Gunners are inundated with top quality options in midfield. Arteta said: “He wasn’t at that level against Brighton, and this is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action, you have to be at that level. “Today was much better. That’s what we have to demand, and this is what I demand to myself. I’m going to demand the same with the players, because if we do that, he will raise the standards and we will be a better team.” Guimaraes was the first player to score twice from the bench this season and both goals have been from outside the box. Figure caption,Guimaraes has ‘perfect’ day despite jet lag ‘The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing’ Arsenal won the league last season in part because of their excellent defence. The Gunners conceded the fewest goals in the league but have already conceded five in six games. The partnership of Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba is one of the best in the world and Arsenal look to be missing the injured Frenchman’s calmness. Ezri Konsa was brought in from Aston Villa for £55m and, despite his quality, is still getting used to his new surroundings. It is unclear how serious Hincapie’s injury is, although he was seen clutching his right ankle as he was carried off by goalkeeper Illan Meslier. He signed for the club on a permanent deal this summer, having initially joined on loan from Bayer Leverkusen last season. Hincapie has suffered from muscular issues this term and now faces an anxious wait to discover whether he requires another spell on the sidelines. Left-back Calafiori, though, has proved integral to Arsenal’s attacking threat. His equaliser against Leeds was his first league strike this term but no defender has been involved in more Premier League goals than the Italian (one goal, two assists). “The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing.” added Arteta. “And we need to be very conscious of that. From being exceptional and being the champions to being extremely average, like in that game, is a really thin line. “So if you don’t want it more than the opponent, you are not able to cope emotionally with certain situations, you’re going to suffer. “And we all suffered and we didn’t enjoy that game, but then you have to learn the lesson and we certainly done that. “We speak about it and you could sense that there was something in those tummies.” Madueke gets chance after attacking struggles Arteta made some big calls when naming his starting XI. He opted to start with German Kai Havertz up front despite the forward returning early from international duty after picking up a hamstring issue, leaving Viktor Gyokeres on the bench again. Gyokeres had scored four goals, registering in every match for Sweden, in the last international break, but looks to have work to do to win his manager round. The 28-year-old has yet to start a Premier League game and in his cameos this season has looked far from the level required as a striker who could fire Arsenal to back-to-back titles. The forward line did not click against Leeds and, with Havertz looking like he lacked match sharpness, thoughts turned towards whether Arsenal missing out on an elite attacker in the summer would haunt them. Winger Christos Tzolis, who has shone at times this season following his summer arrival, suffered a hamstring issue with Greece and, with Eberechi Eze out of form, Arteta used Noni Madueke on the left wing. Madueke was left out of the last England squad due to a lack of minutes with Arsenal but, after “being the best player in training for the last 10 days” according to Arteta, now could be the chance for him to prove his worth.

items.title: Robotique : l’équipe algérienne décroche une médaille d’or au FIRST Global Challenge 2026 en Corée du Sud
items.description: Samsung Electronics Algérie, en partenariat avec Altis Training Center, accompagne l'équipe algérienne qui participera au FIRST Global Challenge 2026, organisé à Incheon, en Corée du Sud, du 7 au 12 octobre 2026. La participation algérienne s’est couronnée avec l’obtention d’une médaille d’or Cette participation réunit cinq lycéens algériens, accompagnés d'un coach et d'un mentor, autour d'une expérience internationale consacrée à la robotique, à l'innovation et aux sciences et technologies. Cinq lycéens algériens au FIRST Global Challenge 2026 grâce à Samsung et Altis Training Center Avant leur départ pour Incheon, l'équipe algérienne a eu l'honneur d'être reçue par Min Kyung-tae, ambassadeur de la Corée en Algérie. Le diplomate sud-coréen a exprimé ses encouragements pour cette « belle représentation de la jeunesse algérienne sur la scène internationale », a indiqué la filiale algérienne du géant sud-coréen de l’électronique et de l’électroménager. En accompagnant les cinq algériens au FIRST Global Challenge 2026, Samsung Electronics Algérie explique qu’elle « souhaite avant tout mettre en lumière le potentiel, la créativité et l'ambition de la jeunesse algérienne, en lui donnant l'opportunité de représenter l'Algérie sur une scène internationale dédiée à l'innovation ». Cette démarche s'inscrit dans une « volonté de contribuer au développement des compétences STEM » et d'encourager une nouvelle génération à « explorer les technologies qui façonneront les métiers et les solutions de demain », ajoute Samsung Algérie. Le FIRST Global Challenge rassemble des jeunes de plus de 190 pays du monde autour de défis de robotique conçus pour mobiliser leurs connaissances scientifiques et technologiques, mais également leur créativité, leur capacité à collaborer et à imaginer des solutions face aux enjeux contemporains. Pour l'équipe algérienne, cette participation constitue bien plus qu'une compétition : elle représente une occasion de confronter ses compétences à un environnement international, d'échanger avec d'autres jeunes talents et de porter le savoir-faire et l'ambition de la jeunesse algérienne au-delà des frontières. Une participation dans un contexte particulier Cette participation prend un relief particulier dans le contexte algérien actuel, marqué récemment par des épisodes climatiques extrêmes, à l'image des feux de forêt ayant touché plusieurs régions du pays. Elle rappelle que les sciences, les technologies et l'innovation constituent, pour la jeunesse algérienne, des leviers essentiels pour comprendre, anticiper et accompagner les réponses aux défis environnementaux auxquels l'Algérie est confrontée. Au-delà de la compétition, l'équipe visitera l'Institut coréen de Recherche Incendie (NFRI) le 12 octobre pour découvrir les technologies avancées de prévention et de gestion des risques incendie. Cette expérience de transfert technologique, organisée par Samsung, offre aux lycéens une compréhension des meilleures pratiques coréennes en la matière. L'accompagnement de l'équipe algérienne repose sur le partenariat entre Samsung Electronics Algérie et Altis Training Center, qui pilote la préparation de l’équipe et assure sa formation, son encadrement pédagogique et son accompagnement technique tout au long du parcours de la préparation en Algérie jusqu’à sa participation au FIRST Global Challenge en Corée du Sud. Samsung s'est associée à Altis Training Center non seulement pour soutenir une compétition mondiale, mais aussi pour investir dans le potentiel des jeunes talents algériens. À travers ce partenariat, Samsung réaffirme son engagement envers l'innovation locale et la formation des futurs leaders technologiques », a déclaré Johnny Jung, Managing Director de Samsung Electronics Algérie, cité dans le communiqué. Le voyage à Incheon et l'accès aux technologies de pointe coréennes représente une opportunité unique d'apprentissage pratique et d'échange technologique. Pour Altis Training Center, ce projet va bien au-delà d’une compétition internationale. Il permet aux jeunes de transformer leurs connaissances en compétences concrètes, de travailler sur des problématiques réelles, de développer leur esprit d’équipe et leur capacité à innover. La société exprime sa fierté d’accompagner les cinq lycéens dans cette « aventure et de contribuer, aux côtés de Samsung, à leur parcours et à l’émergence de jeunes talents algériens ». « La présence de Team Algeria à la FIRST Global Challenge à Incheon prouve ce que les élèves algériens peuvent accomplir avec les bons appuis, et pour cela nous remercions le Ministère de l'Économie de la Connaissance, des Start-up et des Micro-Entreprises ainsi que Samsung pour leur soutien », a souligné Aziza Elkolei, PDG d’Altis Training Center. Aider les jeunes algériens à acquérir les compétences qui façonnent le monde de demain Cette participation entend également contribuer à inspirer d'autres jeunes algériens à s'intéresser davantage aux sciences, aux technologies, à l'ingénierie et à l'innovation, et à envisager ces disciplines comme des leviers de développement et d'avenir. Un engagement qui s'inscrit dans la durée avec Samsung Innovation Campus L'accompagnement de l'équipe algérienne au FIRST Global Challenge s'inscrit plus largement dans les initiatives de Samsung en faveur du développement des compétences technologiques des jeunes. Cette dynamique s'est récemment illustrée à travers le lancement, le 3 octobre 2026, de la nouvelle édition de Samsung Innovation Campus (SIC2026) en Algérie, en partenariat avec l'ESI (École Supérieure d'Informatique), un programme de formation destiné aux étudiants algériens et axé sur le développement de compétences en intelligence artificielle. À travers le FIRST Global Challenge et Samsung Innovation Campus, Samsung Electronics Algérie entend ainsi « contribuer à créer des passerelles entre apprentissage, technologie, innovation et opportunités, afin d'accompagner les jeunes dans l'acquisition des compétences qui façonneront le monde de demain. » L’article Robotique : l’équipe algérienne décroche une médaille d’or au FIRST Global Challenge 2026 en Corée du Sud est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Henderson scores twice as Chelsea thumb Bournemouth
items.description: Jordan Henderson scored his first Chelsea goals to help his new side to a dominant victory over Bournemouth. The 36-year-old midfielder, making his home debut, fired in off the post after just 68 seconds, before adding a second after the break. Joao Pedro also scored twice, while Morgan Rogers was on target. Evanilson pulled one back to briefly give Bournemouth hope at 3-1, but the Cherries remain winless in the Premier League under new manager Marco Rose. Chelsea’s romp began in the second minute when Henderson scored with their first shot of the game, curling a shot in off the inside of the post after being played through by Cole Palmer, who signed a new contract until 2034 in the hours before kick-off. Just 84 seconds later, Henderson played in Rogers, whose cross-shot was flicked over Bournemouth goalkeeper Djordje Petrovic by defender Antonio Silva. Rogers was awarded his fourth goal of the season after a check by the video assistant referee. Having given the ball away too often in the opening few minutes, Bournemouth threatened to pull one back, but Brazilian forward Rayan flashed a shot over before the Cherries briefly began to settle. However, Henderson threatened to extend Chelsea’s lead midway through the half with a lofted effort from the edge of the box. Rayan had another one-on-one effort saved in the 35th minute before Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez denied Ryan Christie at the other end. Bournemouth defender Silva also had a header saved just before half-time. Bournemouth brought on Ben Gannon-Doak at half-time, but 30 seconds later they were 3-0 down. Joao Pedro fired into the top right-hand corner after Pedro Neto reacted well to another Silva mistake in the box. Evanilson pulled one back five minutes later when Moises Caicedo’s clearance ricocheted off him after a dangerous corner fell at his feet inside the six-yard box. But Joao Pedro tapped in a Pep Chavarria cross moments later before Henderson curled a 25-yard free-kick past Petrovic to round off the scoring. Chelsea’s first win in four matches lifts them into the top five. Bournemouth, meanwhile, are only outside of the relegation zone on goal difference. Henderson and Caicedo together at last There was a moment in the 30th minute when Palmer accidentally pushed Ryan Christie into a collision with Caicedo, with the Chelsea midfielder coming off worse. After spending a few moments on the ground, the Ecuador international got to his feet to applause from the Stamford Bridge crowd. The reaction was one of relief from the home supporters, who have been concerned about Chelsea’s midfield options during the opening weeks of the season. Caicedo had played only 14 minutes this season after suffering a recurrence of a calf problem during his substitute appearance against former club Brighton. Meanwhile, his midfield partner Henderson had been recovering from an arm injury sustained at the World Cup with England after he fell awkwardly while jumping over an advertising hoarding during celebrations following a win over Mexico. Having tried four different midfield combinations and named the same pairing in consecutive matches only once, Chelsea were able to start Henderson and Caicedo together for the first time. Henderson impressed during his first full appearance for the club in the win at Brentford before the international break. He was also signed for his leadership qualities as one of three players aged over 30, alongside Danny Welbeck and Emiliano Martinez, recruited to add experience to what had been the Premier League’s youngest squad last season. However, Caicedo is widely regarded as one of Chelsea’s most important players, particularly after the club failed to sign any of their midfield targets on transfer deadline day. Having conceded a league-high 12 goals in their opening five matches before Saturday, Chelsea allowed just one against Bournemouth, their lowest tally in a game against Premier League opposition this season. A clean sheet still eludes them, but manager Xabi Alonso will be encouraged by the greater solidity provided by Caicedo and Henderson in midfield, as an attack featuring Pedro, Rogers and Palmer continues to deliver. Cherries made to pay for mistakes Bournemouth’s winless run had previously been defined by conceding late goals, but early goals were the problem on Saturday. They were arguably unfortunate to fall behind to Henderson’s fine strike, but they were poor in possession throughout the first half and invited pressure. That’s exactly what happened as Rogers curled in Chelsea’s second of the match. Two goals down after two minutes and 30 seconds, it was always going to be difficult to take anything from Chelsea, but another mistake by Silva moments after the interval will be a concern for Rose. It is only the second time Bournemouth have failed to win any of their opening six matches of a Premier League season. The previous occasion came under Rose’s predecessor Andoni Iraola, who went nine games without a win before becoming arguably the most successful manager in the club’s modern history. There are, of course, problems the German coach could not have accounted for as he tries to balance their league form with a first European campaign. He lost star midfielder Alex Scott to injury over the international break after he started his first game for England despite carrying a knock in the build-up to the match. Scott is now expected to be out for up to six weeks, while key attacker Eli Junior Kroupi remains is not due back until November after suffering a significant injury in pre-season. “We played not good so it was a deserved loss, especially if we start how we started in both halves of the game,” said Rose. “We know Chelsea is a team that starts well and scores many goals at the beginning of the game. It’s my fault we didn’t react well to this information. “In the past games, we struggled despite good performances with poor moments. Today, we struggled but had some good moments. “We were not ready, not sharp enough, even our pressing was not Bournemouth-like in many situations. We just didn’t play a good game and this can happen. We need to face the reality of three points from six games.”
